newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish RAKS says BASF broke agreement.
newsitem.headline: Turkish RAKS says BASF broke agreement.

text.p: Turkey's RAKS Holding AS said on Wednesday that BASF broke terms of a letter of understanding between the two companies in deciding to sell its Magnetics unit to South Korean textile group Kohap Ltd.

"BASF didn't conform to the terms of the agreement," RAKS said in a statement. It said the two companies signed an accord in August anticipating the sale to RAKS of BASF Magnetics, one of the world's best known tape brands.
RAKS said that after the accord was signed it had sought more time to gather information on "unclear points" in Magnetics' documents.
"Before this additional period had ended and the necessary information had been collected, BASF AG made the decision to sell...," RAKS said.
BASF said on Tuesday it had sold Magnetics for an undisclosed sum to Kohap.
The chemical giant's supervisory board had expressed concern that the Turkish group was too small and questioned its ability to run Magnetics.
